coordinates.note: Region-grade: the OpenStreetMap point for the village of Zinkgruvan, next to the active zinc mine; the proposed caverns at 1000 m depth have no published coordinate, so the point is good to a few km at best. It lies about 360 km from Lund, as the design report states.

depth.quote: at a depth of 1000 m in the Zinkgruvan mine

name: Zinkgruvan mine (ESSnuSB far detector)
notes: Both the proposed 360 km (Zinkgruvan) and 540 km (Garpenberg) baselines were evaluated; the design report finds the Zinkgruvan option better for measuring delta_CP.

summary.plain: An active zinc mine in central Sweden, about 360 kilometres from Lund, where the ESSnuSB design report proposes to excavate two huge caverns, a kilometre underground, for a 540,000-tonne water detector.
summary.technical: Zinkgruvan mine, the preferred far-detector site (360 km from ESS; Garpenberg at 540 km was the alternative): two caverns 78 m high and 78 m in diameter at 1000 m depth. Attached to the ESS facility record because the far site has no facility of its own in the Atlas.
